გავიხსენოთ: Simple RAG: Answers from Documents

1Why don't we put the whole PDF into the context, and why don't we train the model (fine-tuning)?The whole PDF — thousands of tokens on every question, slow, a large document doesn't fit, “lost in the middle” · fine-tuning — expensive, again on every change, it memorizes facts badly and can't name the source
2What are RAG's two pipelines, and when does each one run?ingestion — once, on upload: PDF → text → parts → vectors → database · query — on every question: vector → top 5 → prompt → an answer with a source
3Why do we cut a document into parts, and what do we need the overlap for?The vector of a whole document is the “average” of everything — blurry; a part = one idea, a precise vector and a cheap context · the overlap — the last sentence in the next part too, so an idea isn't cut at the boundary
4Why do we need a threshold in RAG's search?A search always finds something · without a threshold, for “a borscht recipe” the model would get 5 meaningless parts and might make something up · with a threshold — 0 parts and “I don't have information”
5Why do we store the original question in the chat history and not the message with the sources (augmented)?The sources are only for this request — others will be found next time · storing them in the history would inflate every message with 5 parts (the budget, lecture 7)

RAG ოპტიმიზაცია და შეფასება

🤔რატომ გჭირდებათ

ლექცია 11-ის RAG ზოგჯერ არასწორ ნაწილს პოულობს — განსაკუთრებით ზუსტ სიტყვებზე („B-2“, „12%“). მაგრამ „ზოგჯერ“ ციფრი არ არის, და „მგონი უკეთესია“ არ ითვლება. რეალურ გუნდებში RAG-ის ყოველი ცვლილება — chunking, ძებნის მეთოდი, prompt — გაზომვით მტკიცდება. დღეს ვზომავთ (golden set, hit@k, MRR), ვაუმჯობესებთ (hybrid search, ფილტრი, chunking) და პასუხის groundedness-ს ვამოწმებთ.

🎯ლექციის ბოლოს შეძლებთ

  • ახსნი, სად ცდება RAG (retrieval vs generation), შეადგენ golden set-ს და /rag/eval-ით hit@3-სა და MRR-ს გამოთვლი
  • hybrid search-ს ააწყობ: ვექტორი + PostgreSQL full-text (tsvector, 'simple'), შერწყმული RRF-ით, და გაუმჯობესებას ციფრით დაამტკიცებ
  • metadata filtering-ს SQL-ში დაამატებ და ახსნი, რატომ არის ის უსაფრთხოების საკითხიც
  • chunking-ის სტრატეგიებს და reranking-ს შეადარებ, და პასუხის groundedness-ს GroundednessEvaluator-ით შეაფასებ

დღის თემა

RAG Optimization and Evaluation

🤔რატომ გჭირდებათ

Lecture 11's RAG sometimes finds the wrong part — especially on exact words (“B-2”, “12%”). But “sometimes” isn't a number, and “I think it's better” doesn't count. In real teams every RAG change — chunking, the search method, the prompt — is proven by measurement. Today we measure (golden set, hit@k, MRR), improve (hybrid search, filtering, chunking) and check the answer's groundedness.

🎯ლექციის ბოლოს შეძლებთ

  • You'll explain where RAG fails (retrieval vs generation), put together a golden set and calculate hit@3 and MRR with /rag/eval
  • You'll build hybrid search: the vector + PostgreSQL full-text (tsvector, 'simple'), merged with RRF, and prove the improvement with a number
  • You'll add metadata filtering in SQL and explain why it's also a security matter
  • You'll compare chunking strategies and reranking, and evaluate the answer's groundedness with GroundednessEvaluator

5 კითხვა

1In which two places does RAG fail, and which one is more common?retrieval — the right part didn't get into the top k (the most common; then even the best model can't answer) · generation — the part is right, but the model added something that isn't in the source
2What are hit@3 and MRR? Why do we write a phrase in the golden set and not the chunk's Id?hit@3 — on what share of the questions the right part was in the top three · MRR — the average 1/rank, how high it is · when the chunking changes the Ids change, the phrase doesn't
3Why do we need hybrid search, and why do we merge the lists by rank (RRF) and not by scores?the vector finds exact words (a code, a number, a name) badly, full-text finds them exactly · the scores are in different “units”, the rank is the same everywhere: Σ 1/(60 + rank)
4Why must metadata filtering be in SQL and not in the prompt?the model doesn't always obey the prompt; if someone else's part got into the context, it has already leaked · a tenant/permissions filter is security, before the model
5What is groundedness and how do we measure it? Why don't we trust the judge completely?does the answer rely only on the sources? · LLM-as-judge: GroundednessEvaluator, 1–5 and an explanation · the judge is a model too — it makes mistakes and rates its own answers softly; on many examples and manually from time to time
